title: page-slab allocator: remap fastpath + lockless freelist + pin-policy tuning
author: Aditi Rao
description:
Motivation: large workloads with mixed sequence lengths exposed two runtime inefficiencies in paged KV cache: (1) slow remap path when promoted pages are recycled across arenas, and (2) lock contention on the freelist during high-concurrency continuous-batching spikes. This PR introduces a page-slab allocator that 1) encodes an immutable page header to speed remap checks, 2) switches the primary free list to a lockless, per-cpu slab-backed fastpath with fallback to the global pool, and 3) relaxes the pin/unpin policy to allow ephemeral soft-pins for transient KV prefixes to reduce unnecessary eviction churn.

Summary of changes and rationale:
- Immutable page headers: add compact checksum+flags header at page alloc time to allow O(1) remap validation without walking metadata. This reduces remap cost on hot prefix promotion.
- Lockless per-CPU slabs: new per-worker slab cache implemented with atomic stacks for the common fastpath; removed a hot mutex from the common allocation path. Fallback to global bucket uses coarse-grained lock to keep slow-path rare.
- Soft-pin eviction policy: introduce configurable soft_pin_ttl and a short-lived grace window to avoid immediate eviction of recently-unpinned pages used by streaming/continuous batching.
- Minor: metrics for page churn, lock contention, freelist hit/miss; unit and microbench updates.

Checklist:
- [x] design doc linked (internal)
- [x] unit tests for allocator invariants
- [x] microbench harness for paged allocations
- [x] integration test with continuous-batching smoke
- [x] perf numbers in description below

Benchmark summary: (centroid of 5 runs on c6g.4xlarge-like instance)
- End-to-end latency P50 for streaming long-context mix: down 8-12% (from 21ms -> 18.7ms)
- Tail latency P99: down 18% in steady-state load
- Throughput: +6% sustainable tokens/sec under 99th percentile concurrency
- KV cache hit-rate for hot prefixes: +3.4pp due to reduced premature evictions
- Allocator CPU time measured: allocator kernel path CPU cycles down ~35% in aggregate

Rollout notes:
- Default soft_pin_ttl set to 250ms (config flag runtime.kv.soft_pin_ttl_ms). We will enable feature-flag rollout (console flag: runtime.kv.page_slab_enabled) in canary region for 48h before global rollout.

Observability: added metrics runtime.kv.page_reclaims, runtime.kv.soft_pin_evictions, runtime.kv.percpu_slab_hits.

Testing:
- unit tests for concurrency (race-conditioned)
- added stress test that simulates 4k concurrent short-lived prefix sessions
- microbench harness reports attached commits
- CI initially flaked on sanitizer build due to uninitialized read in test harness; fixed by zero-initing slab headers.

Related: follows on learnings from earlier page-reallocator work but takes a different approach (slab + immutable headers) to avoid coordinated remap stalls. Link to design doc: internal.redwood/eng/kvs/page-slab-allocator/v1 (internal).
